limitations: C25c and AC-74 remain blocked until real Windows and macOS executions are recorded. Linux Node 24/26 execution does not substitute for either OS.

The 29-test Linux Node 26 lifecycle supplement ran at source revision 4413302241d7ff890defb69e3742474edf0559c2 with Node v26.11.1, npm 11.20.0 and Git 2.54.0. The final full-suite capture records its own committed input revision and primary Node 24 environment.
The separate-filesystem test injects EXDEV at the filesystem rename boundary; it is deterministic lifecycle coverage, not a claim of another OS or a real separate-volume run.
Lifecycle tests use disposable isolated homes/projects, Git snapshots and locally packed fake lavish-axi runtimes with offline npm, not real runtime board interactions.
The installer itself still requires its shared JavaScript helpers; target manifest validation is bypassed for owned-link removal.
An existing source runtime differing from the pin is preserved and requires explicit developer preparation. Link removal never deletes source runtime or target content.
Process-interruption tests do not establish power-loss recovery; directory-flush limitations follow the shared recovery writer.
Current-agent invocation/loading remains C26 and real-model acceptance remains C27.
No release, tag, npm publication or hosted CI workflow was created.

Fixture teardown removes task-created disposable homes/projects, source snapshots, npm caches, fake tarballs, stages, links and backups. No task-created dev stack, image or shared cache requires cleanup.
